title: AI disqualification yields new Nikon Small World in Motion winner
gist: Nikon disqualified the winning Small World in Motion video by Ning Xu after allegations of generative AI use and named Nguyen Nam Nhat of Vietnam the new winner. Nikon says it will revisit rules and evaluation procedures as imaging and AI evolve.

insights.claim: Nikon concluded that Ning Xu's winning cilia video did not comply with competition rules on generative AI and moved Nguyen Nam Nhat of Vietnam, with a roundworm and single-celled organism video, into first place.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Concrete case of a major imaging competition policing AI use.
insights.locator: Last month we covered the winner

insights.claim: Researchers flagged structural abnormalities and cell features that appeared and disappeared unlike real cell biology, and others spotted what looked like AI watermarks in the source files.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Illustrates the forensic cues used to spot AI-generated scientific imagery.

insights.claim: Xu said he used AI only to distinguish and visualize features in reconstructed grayscale images, and denied using it to generate the movie, cilia or their motion.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: The line between AI enhancement and AI generation is the contested point and difficult to enforce.
insights.quote: to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images

insights.claim: The other winners moved up a notch: Benedikt Pleyer second, Andrew Moore third, Patrick Hickey fourth and Igor Adameyko fifth.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Housekeeping detail with no market implication.
insights.locator: The other winners also moved up

insights.claim: Nikon Small World in Motion, founded in 2011, is a spinoff of the Small World Photomicrography Competition running since 1974, meant to showcase things seen through the light microscope.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette

insights.claim: Nikon says the decision rests solely on the video's eligibility and is not a judgment of Xu's reputation, scientific contributions or intent.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Careful framing limits legal and reputational exposure for the organizer.

insights.claim: Nikon says the episode shows the need to revisit rules and evaluation procedures, since advances in imaging and AI create new challenges for organizations across many fields.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Expect tighter AI-disclosure rules at image and science competitions and publishers.
insights.quote: This event has shown the need for Nikon Small World and Nikon Small World in Motion to revisit rules and evaluation procedures for future competition entries.
